text: is it you?” said she, turning as I entered. I gave an involuntary start back on seeing her, at which she uttered a short laugh, observing, “I think we are both disappointed.” I came forward and busied myself with the breakfast things. “This is the last day I shall burden your hospitality,” said she, as she seated herself at the table. “Ah, here comes one that will not rejoice at it!” she murmured, half to herself, as Arthur entered the room. He shook hands with her and wished her good-morning: then, looking lovingly in her face, and still retaining her hand in his, murmured pathetically, “The last—last day!” “Yes,” said she with some asperity; “and I rose early to make the best of it—I have been here alone this half-hour, and you—you lazy creature—” “Well, I thought I was early too,” said he; “but,” dropping his voice almost to a whisper, “you see we are not alone.” “We never are,” returned she.
